source_review.notes: Reviewed Princeton and Stanford suffix-array materials, maintained libdivsufsort/libsais and Rust suffix documentation, the primary DC3 linear-work paper, and Carnegie Mellon suffix-array/BWT lecture materials. All eight final destinations returned HTTP 200.

evidence: Checked text T, suffix S_i, n, SA/rank inverse conventions, LCP[0] and predecessor convention, pattern half-open interval, position width, and original versus sentinel-extended length.
Checked symbols, bytes/code points/graphemes, suffix ranks, text coordinates, logical generation, algorithm theorem model, and library contract remain distinct.
notation_and_syntax.notes: Every derived formula states whether the appended sentinel is included.

evidence: Recomputed banana$ SA 6,5,3,1,0,4,2 and adjacent LCP 0,0,1,3,0,0,2.
Recomputed ana interval [2,4), overlapping text positions 1,3, longest repeat ana, and absent xyz empty interval.
Recomputed 21 substring occurrences minus LCP sum 6 equals 15 distinct banana substrings.
Recomputed BWT annb$aa and inverse rotation banana$.
Recomputed mississippi$ exercise SA, rank mapping, LCP, and issi ranks/positions.
numerical_recomputation.notes: Python exact integers do not test 32/64-bit position, byte-size, bucket, or distinct-count overflow.

evidence: Verified prefix-doubling induction: lexicographic rank pairs of two length-L blocks order/equate length-2L prefixes.
Verified Kasai's retained h decreases at most once per text position and successful extensions total O(n).
Verified pattern matches form one contiguous lexicographic suffix interval and plain binary search costs O(|P| log n) symbol comparisons plus output.
Derived distinct substrings by per-suffix prefixes minus adjacent LCP and arbitrary suffix LCP by RMQ minimum over adjacent LCP.
Checked naïve, comparison-doubling, radix-doubling, and linear-time construction claims remain conditional on their stated models.
symbolic_recomputation.notes: No implementation inherits a paper's asymptotic bound without matching its alphabet, RAM, and wrapper behavior.

evidence: Reviewed empty/singleton, all-equal/all-distinct/periodic texts, unique/minimal sentinel, embedded zero, maximum symbol, long common prefixes, and width thresholds.
Reviewed empty/longer/full/suffix/prefix/absent/overlapping patterns, output order, byte-versus-Unicode coordinates, normalization length changes, document separators, and sentinel exclusion.

Reviewed malformed permutation/order/rank/LCP/RMQ/BWT/regions, same-length wrong text generation, arithmetic/allocation overflow, repetitive denial of service, output amplification, partial builds, mapped lifetime, crash publication, and corpus leakage.
boundary_and_adversarial_cases.notes: Permutation-valid arrays remain untrusted until text binding and semantic ordering evidence are established.

evidence: The executable checks SA is a full permutation, adjacent full suffixes are strictly ordered, and SA/rank are exact inverses.
It checks the independently computed LCP vector and reproduces exact prefix interval/positions, repeat, distinct count, BWT, and inverse text.
The chapter specifies independent tiny suffix materialization and cross-algorithm differential validation rather than relying only on construction self-checks.
invariant_checking.notes: The finite trace uses naïve string slicing on banana$ and is not scalable construction or Unicode/persistence evidence.

evidence: Reviewed text/sentinel identity, permutation/order/rank, byte widths, naïve oracle, doubling, induced/difference-cover families, and failure-safe private construction.
Reviewed Kasai/LCP/RMQ, exact prefix boundaries, output coordinates, repeated/distinct/common substring analytics, BWT/FM-index connection, immutability and atomic generations.
Reviewed persistence/text binding/semantic validation, security/resource controls, exhaustive/metamorphic/fault/construction tests, and representative build/query benchmarks.
proof_review.notes: BWT and FM-index capabilities are connections with separate obligations, not automatically complete suffix-array features.

evidence: Doubling, Kasai, contiguous interval, RMQ, distinct-count, and BWT relationships are separately identified and bounded.
Library behavior and construction families are tied to named maintained or academic sources; performance selection is conditional.
The finite banana$ trace is explicitly labeled as a tiny oracle and not production proof.
proof_sketch_labeling.notes: No universal fastest constructor, compressed size, or dynamic update claim is made.

evidence: The standard-library-only Python trace passed exact thirteen-line stdout, empty stderr, and zero exit status under the recorded Python toolchain.
It emits evidence=finite_suffix_array_trace and reproduces suffix order, inverse ranks, LCP, search, overlap, repeat, distinct count, BWT, and inversion.
All eight final external destinations returned HTTP 200 and repository-local links passed module validation.
empirical_evidence_labeling.notes: No scalable doubling/SA-IS/DC3/library build, Unicode coordinate map, fixed-width failure, parallelism, mapping, crash recovery, hostile parser, production memory/cache/tail workload was empirically evaluated.

conceptual_review.notes: Progresses from text/sentinel and semantic permutation through construction families, LCP/Kasai, pattern intervals, substring analytics, BWT/FM-index, immutable generations, persistence, security, and evidence.

practitioner_review.notes: Reviewed byte/code-point coordinate contracts, order-preserving symbol remap, 32/64-bit and peak temporary memory, wrapper/library contracts, result ordering/pagination, normalized-to-original span mapping, immutable segment rebuild, atomic coupled-array publication, mapped-file semantic validation, provenance/access control, repetitive worst cases, and build/query telemetry.

pedagogical_review.notes: Derives the array contract before construction algorithms, distinguishes theorem families from wrappers, gives a fully reproduced banana$ oracle, ten worked examples, and five progressive exercises with complete answers.

limitations: Internal authoring, primary/official-source, mathematical, executable-snippet, conceptual, practitioner, and pedagogical evidence only; no external academic, Princeton, Stanford, Carnegie Mellon, libdivsufsort, libsais, Rust, DC3, BWT/FM-index, Unicode, security, performance, reliability, operations, architecture, or independent practitioner review is claimed. The chapter and finite trace prove neither arbitrary text/canonicalization/coordinate semantics, scalable doubling/SA-IS/DC3/library correctness or asymptotics, fixed-width/allocation/failure safety, RMQ/FM-index correctness, multi-document privacy, concurrent generation safety, durable persistence/crash recovery, hostile-parser security, production memory/cache/NUMA/tail behavior, certification, nor deployment fitness.
